title: Ang 200–218: more Guru Arjan
hookLine: more short hymns of trust and the holy company
tomorrow: what does the ninth Guru say about praise and insult?

lines: A SEED THE SIZE OF A FRECKLE.
cards: A chili seed is about the size of a freckle. You press it into the soil, cover it, water it, and then nothing happens. No signal, no progress bar.
Bebe Jaswant, Simran's grandmother, grows chilies in old paint buckets along the back fence, and she never digs one up to check.
When Simran, sore from a week of parallel parking, asked how she knows they're working, Bebe laughed: you don't know. You water.

teach.h: TRUST: A RESTING, NOT A FEELING.
teach.b: That's close to the word Guru Arjan keeps returning to in the short Gauri hymns from Ang 200 to 218: trust. Not a feeling you summon; a resting.

teach.h: MY SOUL TRUSTS IN THE ONE.
teach.b: One hymn in this stretch says, in paraphrase: the One who owns my body, mind and wealth is wise and knowing; He heard my sorrow and my joy, and my affairs came right; my soul trusts in the One alone.
Notice what he trusts. Not the outcome. The One.
And he doesn't say his sorrows stopped; he says they were heard.
The other thread in these pages is the holy company, the sangat, the people you sing with. Trust comes easier in company, the way a seedling grows straighter tied to a stake. Here's the sense of it.
Trust is something your hands know. A closed fist guards.
An open palm can receive. At the gurdwara, karah prasad, the sweet offering, is received in cupped open hands.
The body learns trust before the mind does. Bebe's buckets are her own small hymn: seed, soil, water, wait. She isn't careless; she waters every evening.
Trust, on this path, isn't doing nothing. It's doing your part, and letting go of the part that was never yours.

how: At the gurdwara, Sikhs receive karah prasad in cupped open hands, and sing Guru Arjan's hymns together in the sangat; trust in the Guru's will, alongside honest effort, is a steady theme of Sikh teaching.

s: trust, in these hymns, means sitting back and doing nothing
Bebe waters every evening: trust is doing your part, then letting go of the rest.
in the hymn, the singer's sorrows simply stop
they're heard, and things come right; he trusts the One, not the outcome.
at the gurdwara, karah prasad is received in cupped, open hands

games.q: your little brother has practiced all week for tomorrow's swim test and still can't sleep. what fits Guru Arjan's trust?
o: you've done your part; now rest, and let tomorrow be tomorrow.
if you trust hard enough, passing is guaranteed.
keep practicing all night; trust means never stopping.
games.why: trust here is resting in the One after doing your part, not a guarantee and not endless effort. seed, soil, water, wait.

practice: Rest your hands in your lap and close them into loose fists; notice the small effort of holding on. Now slowly open them, palms up, and leave them open.
Breathe there, and with each breath out, let your shoulders do what your hands just did.
